mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails in more than 60% of episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals broad-based supply chain weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in the savings rate (proxied by RSAFS YoY change > 1%) signals a flight to safety, reducing risk asset demand and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) above 0.4% for three consecutive months signals improving consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand for goods and services and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in triggered periods, or the mechanism fails in more than 60% of episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.3% in the same month signals a hard landing in the labor market, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.2% AND PAYEMS monthly change < -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in triggered months, or the mechanism fails in more than 50% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on broader GDP growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails in more than 40% of such episodes.
